research_question: Does instructor beauty affect teaching productivity as reflected in student instructional ratings?

ivs.description: Instructor physical appearance rating (average beauty score from six judges, shifted to have mean zero) — the main predictor of interest.

dv.description: Course overall teaching evaluation score (student instructional ratings on a 1-5 scale) — the outcome variable.

controls.description: Instructor age in years — included as a continuous covariate.
Instructor gender (categorical) — control for gender differences.
Instructor minority status (non-Caucasian) — categorical demographic control.
Course credit type (single-credit elective vs more) — categorical course characteristic control.
Course division (lower vs upper) — categorical course-level control.
Instructor native English speaker (yes/no) — categorical control for language background.
Instructor tenure status (on tenure track yes/no) — categorical professional-status control.
Number of students who participated in the evaluation — continuous control for sample size of evaluation.
Number of students enrolled in the course — continuous control for course size.

extracted_analysis.analysis_code:
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

# Load data
path = 'teachingratings.csv'
df = pd.read_csv(path)

# Simple bivariate model
m1 = smf.ols('eval ~ beauty', data=df).fit()

# Model with common controls (categorical variables as factors)
formula = (
    'eval ~ beauty + age + C(gender) + C(minority) + C(credits) + '
    'C(division) + C(native) + C(tenure) + students + allstudents'
)
m2 = smf.ols(formula, data=df).fit(cov_type='HC3')

# Summaries for record
print('Bivariate model: eval ~ beauty')
print(m1.summary().tables[1])
print('\nControlled model (HC3 robust SE):')
print(m2.summary().tables[1])

# Key numbers for conclusion
beauty_coef = m2.params['beauty']
beauty_p = m2.pvalues['beauty']
print(f"\nControlled model beauty coef: {beauty_coef:.4f}, p-value: {beauty_p:.4f}")
